newsitem.title: ITALY: Aeroporti Roma sees bourse quote end-July.
newsitem.headline: Aeroporti Roma sees bourse quote end-July.

text.p: Aeroporti di Roma (ADR), the first Italian airport company to be privatised, expects to be listed on the Milan bourse on July 24 or 25, ADR managing director Gaetano Galia said.
He was speaking to reporters after a presentation to analysts marking the first stage of ADR's pre-sale road show.
Aeroporti di Roma, which is 73.58 percent owned by state industrial holding IRI and runs Rome's two airports at Fiumicino and Ciampino, will make a public sale offer (OPV) on July 15 and 16.
The price per share, in a range of 8,000 to 11,000 lire ($6.44), will be set at a shareholders' meeting on July 12. Italy's Stock Exchange Council has valued the share price at 8,500 lire.
A 41 percent stake of the company's capital will be on offer, with the possibility of up to 45 pct through a "green shoe" option if there is extra demand.
Of the total stake, at least 30 percent will be offered publicly, five percent will be reserved for company employees, and 65 percent will be left for institutional investors.
Lehman Brothers Holdings Plc, Italian bank Imi's LDV Holding B.V., Crediop B.V., UBS Capital B.V. and M.M. Warburg & Co., which indirectly own some 25 pct in the company, will be selling their stake.
With the offer, IRI's stake in Aeroporti di Roma will fall to around 54 pct, but Galia said this was likely to fall further and that by 1998 IRI "will no longer be the main shareholder."
He added that a second tranche sale was planned but the amount had yet to be defined.

The global coordinator for the offer will be Lehman Brothers International (Europe) and co-global coordinator Cofiri Spa, while the OPV will be coordinated by Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino and Crediop.
Aeroporti di Roma boosted its net profits by 61 percent in 1996 to 90 billion lire and increased its turnover 11 percent to 1.16 trillion lire.
